works.title: Crown Ether-Functionalized Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for Precise Monovalent Cation Separation
institutions: Zhejiang University
Zhejiang University , , , ,

works.abstract: Abstract Membrane-based separation offers a highly promising paradigm for the precise extraction of monovalent cations, which is critical for bioinspired engineering and advanced ion-separation applications. However, efficient discrimination among these cations remains profoundly challenging owing to their nearly identical valence states and comparable subnanometer hydrated diameters. Herein, we report the rational design and fabrication of crown ether (CE)-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) membranes that achieve efficient mono/monovalent cation separation while maintaining rapid ion transport. The integration of CE moieties into the framework architectures plays a dual role: narrowing the channels to the angstrom scale while simultaneously serving as specific recognition sites for target cations through host–guest interactions. Consequently, the optimal CE-functionalized TFP-TDA-2 COF membrane exhibits an exceptional K+/Na+ selectivity of 64 with a K+ permeation rate of 41.2 mmol m–2 h–1, surpassing previously reported COF membranes. Theoretical simulations reveal that, while the COF channels provide rapid transport pathway, synergistic CE recognition substantially lowers the thermodynamic dehydration and translocation barrier for K+ relative to Na+. Furthermore, the modular nature of this strategy enables the specific recognition of other targeted cations through precise side-chain engineering by covalently anchoring different crown ether derivatives. This study demonstrates an effective structural engineering strategy for efficient monovalent cation separation, offering an approach for the development of next-generation, single-ion-selective membranes for broad real-world applications.

works.title: Breaking water-structure constraints by Hofmeister effects in interfacial polymerization for polyamide membranes
institutions: Donghua University

works.abstract: Abstract Hydration critically governs the physicochemical behavior of solutes in both the aqueous bulk and interfacial environments. As typical chaotropic Hofmeister ions, weakly hydrated anions (WHAs) can reshape hydration structures and accumulate at water–hydrophobe interfaces. Notably, WHAs paradoxically suppress the solubility of certain small-molecule monomers in water while enhancing that of chemically analogous polymers. Here, we exploit WHA-mediated Hofmeister hydration control to regulate polyamide-forming interfacial polymerization (IP), using the piperazine (PIP) and trimesoyl chloride (TMC) nanofiltration system as the primary model. Introducing WHAs into the aqueous phase reduces the affinity of amine monomers for water and accelerates partitioning into the reaction front in the oil phase, remarkably reinforcing IP self-limitation. Simultaneously, interfacial WHA enrichment lowers interfacial tension and, together with accelerated amine delivery, potentially intensifies transport-driven interfacial instabilities. WHAs also lower interfacial water availability, attenuating acyl chloride hydrolysis. These synergistic effects yield hollow-ridged polyamide selective layers with reduced thickness and high crosslinking density, delivering enhanced water permeance and salt rejection. Crucially, module-scale fabrication of high-performance membranes demonstrates that WHA-mediated Hofmeister hydration control is directly compatible with established desalination pipelines.

works.abstract: Efficient lignin valorization requires not only catalytic depolymerization but also a scalable, aqueous separation route that isolates bioavailable low‐molecular‐weight (LMW) products from recalcitrant oligomers/polymers. Here, oxidative depolymerization of poplar lignin was coupled with cross‐flow nanofiltration using reduced‐graphene‐oxide (rGO) membranes (molecular‐weight cut‐off or MWCO ≈ 470 Da). Across six depolymerization liquors spanning pH 2.5–9.2 and distinct catalytic histories (of polyoxometalate (POM), NaOH, graphene oxide, and control), rGO membranes consistently rejected ≥90% of the >1.6 kDa fraction, while feed pH governed LMW partitioning. Acidic liquors favored a steric‐sieving regime that enriched aliphatic and aromatic monomers in the permeate (separation factors ≈5–6 relative to the high‐MW fraction), whereas alkaline conditions induced electrostatic exclusion, co‐retaining anionic acids with oligomers and suppressing monomer enrichment. Mechanistic studies with model mixtures showed that dilution sharpened selectivity by mitigating concentration polarization and ionic‐strength screening and that aromatics can modulate charge‐based exclusion through competitive interactions within graphitic nanochannels. Continuous diafiltration of the monomer‐rich liquor for 250 h sustained stable flux (~11 ± 1 L m −2 h −1 ) and selectivity, enabling complete recovery of aliphatic and aromatic monomers and LMW fractions while concentrating high‐MW fractions. These results establish rGO membranes as a robust, water‐based separation platform for MW‐resolved lignin fractionation.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing highly permeable polyamide (PA) thin‐film composite (TFC) membranes is a critical pathway for advancing organic solvent nanofiltration (OSN) in industrial chemical separations. Herein, we reported a dual‐regulation strategy utilizing a molecular scaffold to construct PA TFC membrane with enhanced solvent permeance. Acting as a “molecular scaffold”, the –C(CF 3 ) 2 – group of the 2,2‐bis (4‐aminophenyl) hexafluoropropane (BAFP) effectively modulates the packing behavior of PA chains through steric hindrance. Simultaneously, the fluorinated moieties reduce transport resistance by weakening solvent‐membrane interactions. The prepared TFC‐BAFP membrane exhibited an excellent methanol permeance of 20.3 L m −2 h −1 bar −1 , a 3.4‐fold increase over conventional TFC membrane prepared with 4,4'‐diaminodiphenylmethane (MDA). Furthermore, the enhanced rigidity of the BAFP monomer imparted great structural stability and solvent resistance, even under harsh chemical conditions. The TFC‐BAFP membrane also demonstrated efficient sieving for photosensitizer/precursor mixture system and exhibited significantly higher concentration efficiency than the commercial oNF‐2 OSN membrane. This work proposes a molecular engineering strategy for developing highly permeable polyamide OSN membranes by regulating monomer steric hindrance and surface properties, contributing to the advancement of sustainable separation technologies in the chemical and pharmaceutical industries.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial assembly of ionic covalent organic framework (iCOF) membranes remains a significant challenge. In this study, we report the fabrication of freestanding iCOF membranes by manipulating Hofmeister effect during interfacial polymerization (IP) process. Different kinds of inorganic salts are introduced into the aqueous phase to regulate the dissolution and crystallization dynamics of TpPa‐SO 3 H. We discover that Li 2 SO 4 provides the optimal ion‐specific regulation by combining a strongly hydrated anion that effectively dehydrates the growing iCOF and a cation that interacts only weakly with the sulfonate framework, enabling TpPa‐SO 3 H to enrich and stay at the interface. This ion‐specific synergy facilitates the subsequent π–π stacking and ordered assembly into highly crystalline, intact freestanding membranes. The resulting membrane demonstrates a high proton conductivity of 334.7 mS cm −1 at 100°C and 98% RH.

works.abstract: Abstract The pH-responsive two-dimensional nanofiltration membranes enable tunable separation, yet existing membranes suffer from weak charge gating. Herein, we prepared a mica–polyethylenimine membrane using a “coupled charge flip” strategy. The membrane exhibits a strong charge flip (zeta potential from +46.1 to −36.4 mV) across pH 2–12, originating from the synergy between polyethylenimine (zeta potential from +35.2 to +2.5 mV) and mica (zeta potential from −3.1 to −55.7 mV), yielding a charge-flip amplitude (82.5 mV) 41% greater than that of the best performing bipolar pH-responsive membranes. This enables superior pH-dependent molecular gating (e.g., methyl orange) with rejection ranging from 96.98 to 5.03% (pH 2–12) and a gating ratio of 19.28, which is 1.76 times that of the best reported pH-responsive membranes, while maintaining a water permeance of 155 L m–2 h–1 bar–1 and stable cycling over eight pH switches. This work provides a new framework for designing pH-responsive nanofiltration membranes with high gating ratios.

works.title: L-cysteine and maleimide modified acid-resistant poly(amide-sulfonamide) nanofiltration membranes for tetracycline separation
institutions: Tiangong University

works.abstract: Acidic pharmaceutical wastewater containing antibiotics and inorganic salts presents a challenging environmental issue. Conventional polyamide nanofiltration membranes suffer from acid-induced hydrolysis under strongly acidic conditions, resulting in severe performance degradation. Herein, a poly(amide-sulfonamide) nanofiltration membrane was developed via interfacial polymerization using trimesoyl chloride (TMC) as the organic-phase monomer and a mixed aqueous phase containing 3-aminobenzenesulfonamide (ABSA) and L-cysteine (L-Cys). The introduction of L-Cys provided thiol groups for subsequent thiol-maleimide click modification, and maleimide (MAL) post-treatment was employed to regulate the selective layer structure and improve acid stability. The effects of ABSA/L-Cys composition and MAL modification conditions on membrane structure and separation performance were systematically investigated. The optimized membrane achieved complete tetracycline (TC) rejection (100%) and maintained Na 2 SO 4 rejection above 82%. The TC permeance of the ABSA/L-Cys-MAL membrane increased from 7.0 to 14.6 L m −2 h −1 bar −1 while retaining excellent rejection performance. After exposure to 20 wt% H 2 SO 4 for 30 days, the membrane preserved 100% TC rejection, demonstrating superior acid stability and antifouling performance. This study provides a molecular design strategy for developing acid-resistant nanofiltration membranes for challenging acidic antibiotic wastewater treatment.

works.abstract: Abstract Liquid-phase membrane technology for reverse osmosis (RO), nanofiltration (NF), and pervaporation (PV) relies on membranes whose structure and compositionboth the polymeric matrix and the eventually incorporated fillerallow molecules to be discriminated by differences in size (related to diffusivity) and affinity (solubility). Since these technologies have reached commercial maturity, in recent years, further gains in membrane selective diffusivity and solubility have been sought from the use of nanomaterial additives, including porous oxides, zeolites, graphite-based derivatives, and metal−organic frameworks. This review examines, across RO, NF, and PV, which are the key nanomaterials offering the greatest improvements in molecular membrane separation performance for water treatment and discusses the mechanism by which they enhance the separation.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) provide a structurally programmable platform for membrane‐based separation of small‐molecule active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs). Nevertheless, constructing membrane pores with subnanometer precision and resolving structurally similar molecular mixtures remain major challenges. Herein, we report an isoreticular contraction strategy to construct a series of kgd‐topology COF membranes with progressively narrowed apertures in situ on polyacrylonitrile (PAN) substrates through contra‐diffusion interfacial polymerization between hexa(4‐formylphenyl)benzene (HFPB) and three triamine monomers of decreasing size. Systematic framework contraction decreased the aperture from 12.1 to 10.2 Å and then to 6.5 Å, giving molecular weight cut‐offs of 500, 380, and 290 Da, respectively. Notably, membranes with different contraction degrees were further integrated into a cascade separation system with well‐separated molecular‐weight rejection thresholds, enabling the purification of a four‐component mixture of camptothecin‐related compounds with equal mass concentrations, achieving a maximum fraction purity of 96.6%. This work establishes isoreticular contraction as an effective strategy for programming transport‐relevant pores in COF membranes and highlights the potential of kgd‐topology COF membranes for cascade pharmaceutical purification.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Constructing hetero‐structured membranes with well‐defined pore architectures is a promising strategy to enhance gas separation performance, yet achieving structural continuity across different layers remains challenging. Here, we report a hetero‐structured covalent organic framework (COF) membrane featuring graded pores that transition from a microporous selective layer to a mesoporous support. Unlike conventional layer‐by‐layer assembly, our approach employs a pre‐adsorption‐induced heteroepitaxial growth strategy, wherein hydrazine monomers are electrostatically pre‐organized within the channels of a sulfonated COF scaffold (TpBD‐SO 3 H). This spatial confinement directs the nucleation and growth of the secondary COF layer (TpHz), creating a chemically integrated and robust interface with a continuous pore size transition from 0.9 nm to 2.5 nm, as evidenced by an intermediate pore size of 1.9 nm arising from partial channel penetration. The resulting membrane exhibits an H 2 permeance of 1854 GPU and an H 2 /CO 2 selectivity of 15, surpassing the 2008 Robeson upper bound. This work demonstrates that graded pore engineering offers an effective route to combine high permeability with molecular sieving precision in crystalline membrane design.

works.title: Pressure and Cross-Flow Dependent Interfacial Fouling of Mesoporous PES-PUMA Membranes During Water-in-Oil Emulsion Separation

works.abstract: Water-in-oil (W/O) emulsion treatment is challenging because efficient membrane separation requires simultaneous control of oil transport, water rejection, interfacial interactions, and fouling resistance. However, the coupled effects of operating pressure and cross-flow hydrodynamics on membrane pore accessibility, foulant-layer evolution, and the permeability-rejection trade-off during cyclic W/O emulsion treatment remain insufficiently understood. In this study, an electrospun mesoporous polyurethane–melamine/polyethersulfone (PES-PUMA) membrane was evaluated for the separation of stabilized W/O emulsions under different operating pressures and feed flow rates. At an ultra-low pressure of 20 kPa, the membrane achieved an oil permeate flux of 36.5 ± 2.7 L m−2 h−1 and water rejection of 93.1 ± 2.1%. Increasing the operating pressure to 100 kPa increased the oil permeate flux to 87.6 ± 3.5 L m−2 h−1 while decreasing water rejection to 78.2 ± 1.8%. Increasing the cross-flow rate from 0.05 to 0.5 mL s−1 increased the oil permeate flux from 23.4 ± 0.7 to 90.7 ± 2.1 L m−2 h−1 while decreasing water rejection from 95.3 ± 2.1% to 78.4 ± 1.2%. Quadratic regression models revealed significant nonlinear relationships between hydraulic operating conditions and both separation responses, providing a quantitative description of the pressure- and flow-dependent performance trade-off. Higher cross-flow reduced foulant-layer thickness and favored more reversible fouling, whereas increasing operating pressure promoted pore constriction and compact foulant deposition. These findings establish a quantitative pressure–cross-flow–transport–fouling relationship, demonstrating that hydraulic conditions jointly regulate membrane permeability, water rejection, foulant-layer development, and fouling reversibility. This study therefore provides mechanistic and quantitative insight into optimizing the operation of the established PES–PUMA membrane to balance separation performance and fouling resistance during W/O emulsion treatment.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving high ion selectivity, low membrane resistance, and long‐term stability remains a key challenge in developing two‐dimensional nanomaterial polymer composite membranes, where interfacial interactions critically influence membrane structure and ion transport. Here, we report interfacially regulated MXene‐based nanocomposite membranes in which humic acid (HA) mediates interactions between Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene nanosheets and a sulfonated polyethersulfone matrix. Structural characterization together with molecular dynamics simulations indicates that HA incorporation modifies MXene organization and interfacial interactions within the membrane, which are associated with enhanced ion‐transport properties. The optimized membrane achieved near‐ideal monovalent cation selectivity (∼99%), a low area‐specific membrane resistance of 0.06 Ω·m 2 , and an energy conversion efficiency of 45.6%. The same membrane was evaluated over multiple electrochemical testing cycles totaling approximately 300 h, including dedicated 48 h stability measurements under heavy‐metal‐ and organic‐foulant‐containing conditions. A model‐based assessment of a conceptual reverse electrodialysis (RED) stack predicts a 37% increase in power generation, accompanied by an increase in energy conversion efficiency from 30.0% to 41.1%, relative to the commercial‐membrane scenario. These findings demonstrate that regulating interfacial interactions provides an effective design strategy for developing MXene‐based ion‐selective membranes for salinity‐gradient energy harvesting and related electrochemical separation processes.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Graphical abstract illustrating a novel multi-pass concentric membrane distillation module designed for treating saline water and wastewater. The illustration shows the three-dimensional module assembly, exploded view of its components, and schematic representation of the concentric flow channels, including feed circulation through the inner and outer shells and vapor/permeate collection. The proposed configuration enables feed recirculation and efficient membrane utilization, offering a compact, energy-efficient, versatile design with improved permeate flux for water purification and desalination applications. Although membrane distillation (MD) is widely applied in desalination and wastewater treatment, its industrial-scale implementation remains limited due to low permeation flux caused by inefficient membrane module design. This necessitates the development of better designs for MD modules that address the drawbacks of traditional MD module designs, including limited flexibility, low compactness, design complexity, and performance limitations. In this study, a multi-pass concentric tubular module for the MD process is presented for desalination and wastewater treatment. The developed module offers a simple design with enhanced efficiency, flexibility, and compactness, enabling integration of vacuum MD and direct-contact MD functionalities within a single unit. The module uses flat-sheet membranes, resulting in high packing density, scalability, and energy efficiency. Further, the module incorporates a multi-pass feed recirculation technique and low-conductivity construction materials, resulting in improved heat and mass transfer efficiency. The module is also capable of treating two different feed streams simultaneously using a multi-feed configuration with a single permeate stream. Moreover, different membranes can be mounted on the inner and middle shells based on feed quality and requirements. The application of the module has been demonstrated by treating saline water, textile, and pharmaceutical wastewater to establish the robustness of the proposed design. The developed module demonstrated stable performance, achieving permeate fluxes of 5.63 L m−2 h−1 in vacuum MD mode and 4.95 L m−2 h−1 in direct-contact MD mode, with high salt rejection (&gt;99%).

institutions: Freie Universität Berlin

works.abstract: Abstract Reprogramming the transport preference of crystalline membranes offers a useful strategy for adapting a single membrane platform to different gas-separation tasks. Herein, we report ionic liquid (IL) engineering of pure ZIF-8 membranes to switch H2/CO2 transport from H2- to CO2-preferential behavior. A continuous ZIF-8 membrane was first fabricated on an anodic aluminum oxide support by cathodic deposition, followed by the loading of an IL of type 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide ([BMIM][TFSI]). The compact, well-intergrown, and crystalline ZIF-8 membrane was preserved after IL incorporation, and vibrational spectroscopy provided evidence for molecular interactions between confined [BMIM][TFSI] and the ZIF-8 framework. Gas-permeation measurements revealed that increasing IL loading decreased both H2 and CO2 permeances, indicating an increased transport resistance caused by partial pore occupation. However, the H2 permeance decreased significantly more rapidly than the CO2 permeance. The H2/CO2 selectivity decreased from 3.6 for the pristine ZIF-8 membrane to approximately 0.3 at 15 vol % ionic-liquid loading, corresponding to a CO2/H2 selectivity close to 3. The separation reversal originates from the combined effects of IL-induced pore narrowing and preferential CO2 affinity. This work demonstrates that confined ILs can reprogram adsorption–diffusion coupling in MOF membranes and provides a route toward process-adaptive gas-separation membranes.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT The 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, awarded for pioneering contributions to metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), underscores their revolutionary impact and growing importance in advanced separation technologies. Hybrid porous media that integrate crystalline MOFs within polyimide matrices represent a state‐of‐the‐art platform for tackling the global water‐energy nexus. Nevertheless, their practical performance is often constrained by interfacial incompatibility and inherent structural trade‐offs between rigidity and flexibility. This review establishes a unified “rigid‐flexible coupling” design paradigm, systematically dissecting interfacial engineering strategies that convert weak physical interactions into chemically welded interfaces via covalent grafting, hydrogen bonding, and defect‐mediated coordination. Particular focus is given to the dimensional evolution from two‐dimensional mixed‐matrix membranes to three‐dimensional hierarchical aerogels, which signifies a pivotal shift in mass transport from diffusion‐controlled to convection‐dominated regimes. Building on this framework, the review elucidates how hierarchical architectures enable multifunctional capabilities, including selective ion separation through Donnan exclusion, Janus‐wettability‐governed multiphase separation, and photothermal‐assisted remediation of high‐viscosity crude oil. Finally, it distills materials design principles and discusses emerging frontiers in artificial‐intelligence‐driven materials discovery and four‐dimensional‐responsive systems. By bridging interfacial chemistry, structural hierarchy, and transport physics, this review offers a comprehensive blueprint for the rational design of next‐generation hybrid porous media for sustainable environmental technologies.

works.abstract: Science is commonly divided into fundamental and applied research. In this review we set out to trace the mutual influence of these two facets of scientific work in the field of membranes. The history of applications of membrane science spans only a few decades. In the 1950s and 1960s, relatively simple notions of ion and molecule motion in a membrane—treated as point charges interacting with a charged matrix solely through electrostatic and friction forces—matched both the relatively simple structure of the membranes themselves and the processes of desalination and concentration. Today a membrane is often a miniature reactor in which chemical transformations are coupled with the simultaneous separation of the reaction products. This short review considers current views on the mechanisms of transport and selective separation that take into account membrane structure at the nanometre scale and the contributions of forces of different nature. Our analysis shows that (1) tuning the interplay of the energy barriers of different nature (electrostatic, steric, dielectric and dehydration) opens the way to membranes selective towards a specific ion; (2) the conductivity–selectivity trade-off is an empirical tendency that can be circumvented by tailoring the membrane nanostructure; (3) membranes are evolving from passive barriers towards multifunctional systems in which transport is coupled with chemical reactions, electronic conduction or a second driving force; (4) the demands of applications such as lithium and ammonium recovery increasingly drive the study of transport mechanisms.

works.title: Advances in conductive membrane technologies for sustainable recycling of lithium-ion batteries from electric vehicles
institutions: Universiti Teknologi MARA
works.abstract: The rapid expansion of the electric vehicle (EV) sector has markedly escalated the manufacturing and utilization of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), hence producing a continually rising amount of end-of-life (EoL) battery waste. LIB include precious metals such as lithium, cobalt, nickel, and manganese, the extraction of which from basic sources entails significant ecological repercussions and financial expenditures. Traditional recycling methods, especially pyrometallurgical and hydrometallurgical techniques, are often used; yet they include several drawbacks, such as elevated energy usage, reliance on toxic substances, and the production of secondary waste and contaminants. Consequently, there is an immediate need to advance environmentally friendly, more effective, and sustainable recycling technology. Membrane-based separation has surfaced as a viable option due to its comparatively low energy demands, ease of operation, and capacity for eco-friendly processing. This assessment rigorously examines the function of membrane technologies in the recycling of LIB, focusing specifically on their capacity to selectively extract precious metal ions from intricate battery leachates. Emphasis is placed on conductive membranes that combine electrochemical properties with membrane separation to improve ion selectivity, transport, and recovery efficacy. Notwithstanding these benefits, membrane systems encounter several obstacles, including as membrane fouling, restricted selectivity in multicomponent systems, concentration polarization, membrane deterioration, and difficulty related to large-scale deployment. Recent progress in material engineering, such as nanocomposite membranes, conductive membranes, and hybrid electro-membrane systems, presents significant opportunities to address these constraints. This evaluation highlights the prospects and obstacles linked to membrane technologies and examines their possible incorporation with supplementary processes in sophisticated battery-recycling systems. In conclusion, the creation of efficient, selective, resilient, and scalable membrane systems is vital for the sustainable extraction of crucial materials and facilitating the shift to a circular economy in the swiftly growing electric vehicle battery industry. • Integration of electrochemical functionality with membrane separation enhances ion selectivity and transport, particularly in complex multi-ion battery leachates. • Advanced materials such as graphene, carbon nanotubes, and MXenes significantly improve membrane performance in terms of conductivity, permeability, and selectivity. • Hybrid systems (e.g., electro-membrane crystallization) enable simultaneous separation and recovery, reducing process steps and reagent demand. • Key challenges remain, including membrane fouling, scalability, and cost, requiring further innovation and system integration for industrial application.

works.title: Polyamidoamine Demulsifier-Functionalized Polyvinylidene Fluoride Microfiltration Membrane for Antifouling Oil/Water Emulsion Separation
institutions: Soochow University , , ,
China National Offshore Oil Corporation EnerTech , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract The treatment of oily wastewater has emerged as a critical environmental issue due to the prevalence of oil spills and the discharge of industrial organic pollutants. However, membrane fouling is a major challenge for conventional separation methods, leading to the decreased efficiency and increased maintenance costs. Single hydrophilic modification offers an opportunity to prevent oil fouling but fails to avoid severe permeate flux decline. Herein, we propose a strategy to integrate demulsification and hydrophilicity to a single membrane via incorporation of the polyamidoamine (PAMAM) demulsifier into the hydrophilic tannic acid (TA)-modified membrane through the Schiff base reaction, aiming to alleviate membrane fouling and flux decline during oil/water emulsion separation. The synergy between demulsification and hydrophilicity establishes an oil-repellent barrier surface to prevent oil droplet adhesion on the membrane surface or being squeezed into the membrane pores. When separating oil/water emulsions, the membranes not only showed high separation efficiency with oil content less than 8 ppm in filtrate but demonstrated outstanding antifouling performance with low flux decline ratio (DRt) of 16% even at the high permeate flux of 3679 L m–2 h–1 bar–1, while showing a flux recovery ratio as high as 99.6%, hard to achieve by traditional hydrophilic membranes. In addition, the effect of surface roughness on the demulsification and antifouling separation performance of membranes was also investigated by introducing SiO2 nanoparticles to create a rougher surface. The TA/SiO2-PAMAM membrane with rougher surface exhibited a higher flux DRt of 28%, while showing better demulsification performance with smaller droplet size (∼0.8 nm) in filtrate. This research paves the way for designing membranes for continuous and stable oil/water emulsion separation.

works.abstract: As a critical energy-saving component in reverse osmosis desalination systems, turbine-type energy recovery devices require rigorous dynamic stability evaluation. To guarantee the safety and stability of these devices, this study employs free and constrained modal analyses of its rotor components using Ansys Workbench. The critical speeds, natural frequencies, and other pertinent parameters of the rotor under various rotational speeds and material properties are calculated. Additionally, the dynamic characteristics of rotors crafted from polyethylene, gray cast iron, stainless steel, structural steel, and 40Cr are examined. The findings reveal that the first six natural frequencies of the rotor in free mode are nearly zero, with the natural frequencies progressively increasing from the 7th to 12th modes, accompanied by varying degrees of deformation. Under constrained conditions, the modes of a turbine-type energy recovery device exhibit stability and are less susceptible to resonance. As the rotational speed varies, the natural frequencies of the modes gradually increase, with critical speeds emerging solely in the first three modes, specifically 93 336, 1.1786 × 105, and 1.3139 × 105 rpm, respectively. Furthermore, as the density and Young’s modulus of the rotor material increase, the first three critical speeds also exhibit a continuous upward trend. This research provides a foundational design basis for the structural stability of turbine-type energy recovery integrated machines.

works.abstract: In this study, β-FeOOH and graphite nanosheets (GNSs) were deposited on the surface of cellulose acetate membrane by vacuum filtration method to prepare a cellulose acetate-based composite membrane, β-FeOOH/GNS-1. β-FeOOH/GNS-1 was applied to treat the oil-in-water emulsions, including those consisting of n-hexane, toluene, waste cooking oil (WCO), 1,2-dichloroethane, and petroleum ether. β-FeOOH/GNS-1 achieved an oil-water separation efficiency higher than 99% and a flux exceeding 600 L m−2 h−1 bar−1. Additionally, β-FeOOH/GNS-1 possesses a photo-Fenton self-cleaning function. When β-FeOOH/GNS-1 was applied for the photo-Fenton degradation of methylene blue, a degradation efficiency of 98% was obtained. Meanwhile, after undergoing five consecutive cycles of oil separation from the emulsion of WCO, β-FeOOH/GNS-1 retained an oil separation efficiency above 98%. Therefore, β-FeOOH/GNS-1 exhibited good emulsion separation performance and photo-Fenton catalytic activity, positioning it as a promising membrane material for wastewater treatment application.

works.abstract: Surface engineering is pivotal for tailoring membranes to complex water treatment processes, yet conventional strategies often involve multiple steps, toxic reagents, structural alteration, or specialized equipment. Here, we report a rapid, green, and universal surface modification strategy using Fenton-catalyzed hydrogel coating. Within minutes, an ultrathin cross-linked polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) network forms on porous membranes with diverse chemistries, pore sizes, and surface properties without altering their original pore architecture or porosity. The robust coating resists acid, alkali, heat, ultrasonication, and repeated folding. It enhances hydrophilicity, underwater superoleophobicity, and antifouling performance against oil-in-water emulsions, humic acid, and bovine serum albumin. The PVP network also enables uniform and stable deposition of carbon nanotubes, graphitic carbon nitride, MXene nanosheets, and titanium dioxide nanoparticles. The resulting composite membranes exhibit excellent long-term desalination performance. This simple, scalable, and eco-friendly platform provides a versatile route to advanced functional membranes for sustainable water treatment and resource recovery. Surface engineering is pivotal for designing water treatment membranes, though often requires unfavorable reagents and complex, time consuming procedures. Here, the authors develop a rapid and green surface-engineering strategy based on a modified polyvinylpyrrolidone network for water treatment membranes.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Due to its high energy conversion efficiency and broad accessibility to solar energy, interfacial solar steam generation presents a promising, and cost‐effective solution for desalination of saline water. However, salt accumulation on evaporator surfaces remains a major challenge, especially in the case of high‐salinity environments as the blockage it creates significantly hinders the efficiency as well as continuity of the evaporation process. Salt accumulation also significantly degrades the evaporator's surface over time, reducing its performance and efficiency. Researchers have explored various strategies, including surface modifications, hierarchical structural designs, and anti‐scaling coatings on evaporators. Despite promising results, achieving an optimal balance between maximum evaporation rates and energy efficiency remains a complex and ongoing challenge in this field of research. This study introduces tailor‐designed cylindrical MXene/aramid nanofiber aerogels as self‐cleaning solar evaporators that tolerate high salinity conditions and achieve evaporation rates of up to ∼2.26 kg m −2 h −1 at ∼80% efficiency. This self‐rotating photothermal evaporator exhibits periodic self‐regeneration rotation triggered by accumulated salt crystals to maintain its efficiency and performance. These findings represent a substantial advancement in solar thermal desalination technology for real‐world applications and provide a sustainable solution for efficient water purification, particularly in high‐salinity environments.

works.abstract: Membrane separation is central to potable water production, wastewater reclamation, desalination, gas separation, and decarbonization, yet its economics remain constrained by fouling and by a gap between process data and timely operating decisions. Digital twins (DTs) offer live, bidirectionally coupled virtual representations of physical assets, while machine learning (ML) extracts predictive and prescriptive insights from operational data. Together, they are promising computational approaches for membrane systems. However, their applications have largely evolved independently across fouling prediction, DT development, and ML-based materials discovery. This review argues that these are converging strands of a single trajectory toward self-sensing, self-predicting, and eventually self-designing membrane systems, and that treating them separately obscures key interdependencies. The contributions are threefold. First, applying the digital model/digital shadow/digital twin taxonomy, it shows that most published membrane DTs are digital shadows (DSs). Second, it proposes a five-level autonomy framework, inspired by vehicle automation taxonomies, providing a unified scale for comparing applications ranging from LSTM-based fouling forecasting and reinforcement learning dosing control to autonomous materials laboratories. Third, it integrates autonomous materials design, including self-driving laboratories, inverse design, generative models, and Bayesian search, into the upper levels of this ladder. Evidence is synthesized across reverse osmosis, nanofiltration, ultrafiltration, microfiltration, membrane bioreactors, membrane distillation, and gas separation membranes, with emphasis on critically assessing model performance and generalizability. The study concludes with a roadmap for overcoming data limitations, poor interpretability, interoperability gaps, cybersecurity risks, techno-economic barriers, and regulatory trust deficits that block autonomous membrane systems.

works.abstract: Quartz and feldspar are used in a range of industrial applications owing to their distinct physicochemical properties. However, their selective separation remains challenging because of the similar bulk and surface physicochemical properties. Froth flotation has become the principal approach for quartz–feldspar separation, whereas conventional hydrofluoric acid-based processes are increasingly restricted by their toxicity, corrosivity, and environmental impacts. This review critically summarized the development of quartz–feldspar flotation from traditional HF systems to fluoride-free acidic processes and emerging fluoride- and acid-free technologies. Particular attention was given to the flotation behavior and adsorption mechanisms of cationic, anionic, and mixed cationic/anionic collectors under different pH conditions. The roles of surface charge, active sites, electrostatic interactions, hydrogen bonding, chemisorption, and synergistic adsorption in governing flotation selectivity were systematically discussed. Recent advances emphasized reduced reliance on HF and molecular-level regulation of mineral interfaces. However, laboratory selectivity does not by itself establish industrial applicability. This review also evaluated constraints imposed by fine particles, slimes, impurities, dissolved ions, recycled process water, and incomplete liberation, and identifies priorities for pilot- and plant-scale validation of promising fluoride-free and acid-free systems.

works.abstract: Industrial wastewater poses a serious environmental challenge, as the discharge of large amounts of organic dyes threatens aquatic ecosystems and human health. Accordingly, certain two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials, such as graphene, MXenes, and molybdenum disulfide, have demonstrated considerable potential for the efficient removal of organic dyes. Their high specific surface area, tunable interlayer spacing, and abundant surface functional groups offer significant advantages in dye adsorption and membrane separation applications. This review examines the adsorption efficiency, removal mechanisms, membrane separation performance, and recyclability of selected 2D nanomaterials for the treatment of industrial dye wastewater. Notably, particular emphasis is placed on the influence of material structural characteristics on dye removal. Furthermore, the effects of different environmental conditions on removal mechanisms, membrane fouling behavior, and long-term operational stability are also discussed. Additionally, environmental accumulation, ecological toxicity, eco-friendly synthesis, and sustainable development strategies are discussed. The paper highlights current research limitations and future directions, providing a theoretical foundation for the efficient and environmentally friendly application of 2D nanomaterials in water treatment.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven interfacial evaporation is a promising solution to freshwater scarcity, yet it faces bottlenecks regarding salt accumulation, limited evaporation modes, and single functionality. Here, inspired by plant vascular tissues, we have developed a 3D core–shell Janus hydrogel evaporator to achieve the synergy of high‐efficiency freshwater production and stable hydrovoltaic energy harvesting. To construct this core–shell architecture, an alkali‐induced dehydroflurination strategy is employed to solve the bonding challenge between hydrophobic poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) and the hydrophilic sodium alginate (SA) core, while simultaneously triggering the in situ oxidation of manganese ions to form MnO 2 , thus conferring antibacterial activity on the device. The PVA/chitosan shell and sodium alginate core are endowed with bio‐inspired vascular channels through a foaming and freeze‐thawing process, which ensures efficient water transport and salt resistance. Crucially, this design leverages the tunable water‐content environment within the hydrogel and the water‐polymer interactions to enable a unique “Hydrogel/Janus dual‐core” evaporation mechanism. Furthermore, the incorporation of dodecasodium phytate markedly enhances the surface charge density, yielding an evaporation rate of 4.22 kg m − 2 h − 1 under one sun and a sustained output voltage of 825 mV in seawater. This bioinspired all‐in‐one platform offers a pathway from passive solar distillation to active water‐energy synergy.

works.title: Defect- and Composite-Engineered Free-Standing Nanoporous Graphene Film for High-Efficiency Solar-Driven Water Evaporation
institutions: Harbin Institute of Technology , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Solar-driven interfacial evaporation has emerged as a promising strategy for sustainable freshwater production. However, simultaneously achieving efficient photothermal conversion and optimized water transport within a single material system remains challenging. Herein, three-dimensional (3D) nitrogen-doped nanoporous graphene (NG) with tunable microstructures is synthesized by tuning the composition of Ni-based nanoporous templates via chemical vapor deposition (CVD). The defect density of the CVD-grown NG clearly increases with the number of components (or entropy) of the nanoporous alloys, reducing thermal conductivity, and promoting heat localization. Furthermore, when Mo element is included in the nanoporous alloy template (np-MnNiCoFeMo), MoC forms during CVD, inducing secondary nanoholes on the graphene tube walls and creating more defects. By selectively removing the alloy template, the obtained nanoporous graphene/MoC composite (5-NG@MoC) exhibits synergistically enhanced photothermal conversion due to the combined light absorption from both components of the composite. Consequently, 5-NG@MoC achieves a broadband solar absorption of 94% (250–2500 nm) and delivers an evaporation rate of 1.76 kg·m–2·h–1 with a photothermal conversion efficiency of 92.8% under one-sun irradiation. The free-standing and ultralight composite also demonstrates excellent stability and salt resistance during seawater desalination. This work provides an effective strategy for engineering graphene-based photothermal materials toward high-efficiency water evaporation.

works.title: Precious or Base Metals? A Sustainability Assessment of Catalytic Strategies in Chemical Synthesis
institutions: Politecnico di Milano
works.abstract: Abstract The widespread use of precious-metal catalysts has enabled highly efficient fine chemical syntheses but has also intensified concerns over critical raw material dependence, catalyst cost, and the environmental burdens associated with their production. Although catalyst recycling and substitution with base metals are increasingly proposed as circularity strategies, their economic and environmental trade-offs have rarely been evaluated at the process level. Here, we develop an integrated techno-economic assessment (TEA) and life-cycle assessment (LCA) framework to compare three catalyst-management strategies: conventional precious-metal catalysis, precious-metal catalysis with catalyst recycling through organic solvent nanofiltration, and base-metal catalysts. Five industrially relevant fine chemical syntheses encompassing pharmaceutical active ingredients and high-value intermediates were selected as representative case studies. Catalyst recycling reduced catalyst demand while requiring only a moderate increase in capital expenditure and lowering operating costs and environmental impacts relative to conventional precious-metal catalysis. Base-metal substitution delivered the largest overall improvements, decreasing average capital expenditure by ca. 8%, operating costs by up to 28%, and carbon emissions by 25%, mitigating planetary-boundary and endpoint environmental impacts. Thus, base-metal catalyst substitution emerged as the preferred long-term strategy for advancing catalyst circularity. Importantly, sensitivity analysis identified catalytic performance as a decisive design parameter: base-metal substitution remained advantageous when catalytic activity is maintained within approximately 15% of the precious-metal benchmark, whereas larger activity losses could shift the preferred strategy toward recycling the precious-metal catalyst. These results establish a process-level framework for catalyst circularity and show that recycling and base-metal substitution are complementary rather than competing strategies.

works.title: Near-exact resistance of an orifice in a 2D membrane blocked by a cylindrical obstruction
institutions: Department of Physics, University of Ottawa , 150 Louis-Pasteur Private, Ottawa, Ontario K1N 6N5,
works.abstract: A near-exact analytical expression is presented for the Ohmic resistance of an orifice in a 2D membrane separating two infinitely large conductive reservoirs and obstructed by an infinitely long cylinder. The expression is obtained by constructing a curvilinear coordinate system adapted to the obstructed geometry, with constant-coordinate surfaces mapping the system boundaries, and by integrating the resistive contributions of infinitesimally thin constant-coordinate slices. Although these surfaces do not correspond exactly to equipotential surfaces, the resulting expression provides a rigorous lower bound on the resistance and deviates from the exact resistance by &lt;0.17% over the full range of admissible obstruction sizes. This near-exact expression can further be used to model the access region of obstructed finite-length cylindrical channels, providing an analytical tool for single-molecule sensing applications.

works.title: An Ultrathin Ionic COF Self‐Supporting Proton Exchange Membrane Through Stacking of Few‐Layer Nanosheets Grown From High‐Curvature Micro‐Interface for Fuel Cell
institutions: Dalian University of Technology
State Key Laboratory of Fine Chemicals
State Key Laboratory of Fine Chemicals Frontier Science Center for Smart Materials School of Chemical Engineering Dalian University of Technology Dalian China
School of Chemical Engineering Ocean and Life Sciences Dalian University of Technology Panjin China
Panjin Institute of Industrial Technology Dalian University of Technology Panjin China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Ultrathin self‐supporting ionic covalent organic framework (iCOF) proton exchange membranes (PEM) are crucial for low‐resistance sustainable energy applications but remain challenging to fabricate. The key to fabricating ultrathin self‐supporting iCOF membranes lies in the compact stacking of iCOF nanosheets, which remains inaccessible through micro‐interfacial polymerization systems. Herein, we report for the first time an ultrathin self‐supporting iCOF PEM constructed by growing few‐layer iCOF nanosheets at high‐curvature micro‐interfaces, alongside a proposed growth mechanism. The curved iCOF exhibits reduced interlayer attraction due to a twisted configuration, and enhanced solvation‐driven exfoliation arising from greater exposure of sulfonic acid groups to water. It avoids the commonly reported nanosphere‐like morphologies in previously reported micro‐interfacial assembly systems by regulating the oil‐in‐water microemulsion interface using weakly surface‐active octanoic acid, which effectively balances between the confined oil phase growth and the unconfined aqueous phase exfoliation. As‐prepared iCOF few‐layer nanosheets (1.3–1.5 nm) expose abundant reactive terminal groups for interlayer crosslinking under the vacuum filtration pressure gradient, leading to ultrathin self‐supporting iCOF PEM (3.2–15.1 µm) with compact layer stacking, good mechanical robustness, and excellent scalability (20 cm in diameter). A fuel cell peak power density of 2017.7 mW cm −2 at 80°C is achieved, surpassing recently reported iCOF‐based membranes.

works.title: Halide Identity Shapes Ion Pairing and Solvent Dynamics in Aqueous Lithium Halide Electrolytes
works.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
institutions: Kansas State University , , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Predicting whether electrolytes associate or dissociate in water is challenging because direct ion attraction, hydration, solvent caging, and collective reorganization operate on comparable free-energy scales, and subtle changes in their balance can reverse the preferred ion-pairing state. Here, we develop machine-learned potentials trained on density-corrected r2SCAN to investigate how periodic trends across the halide series govern the thermodynamics, structure, and dynamics of aqueous lithium halide electrolytes. The resulting potentials of mean force reveal a systematic shift from the strongly stabilized contact ion pair in LiF toward solvent-shared and dissociated configurations for LiCl, LiBr, and LiI, with apparent dissociation constants spanning nearly 4 orders of magnitude. This thermodynamic progression emerges from the balance among direct ion attraction, hydration shell stability, solvent caging, and water-mediated screening. From F– to I–, the halide hydration shell becomes increasingly diffuse and labile, with faster water exchange and orientational relaxation. These changes provide a microscopic dynamical basis for the progression from structure-making to structure-breaking behavior, accompanied by a shift from strongly suppressed toward modestly enhanced water mobility. The same hydration contrast governs the coupling between ion separation and solvent reorganization during association and dissociation. Together, these results establish a unified molecular connection among association–dissociation equilibria, hydration shell dynamics, and solvent transport in aqueous electrolytes.

works.title: Three-dimensional particle-fluid hybrid simulation of multi-cathode-spot jet mixing and ion separation in vacuum arcs
institutions: Hefei University of Technology
Institute of Applied Physics and Computational Mathematics
works.abstract: Abstract Supersonic plasma jets generated by multi-component cathodes in vacuum arcs critically influence the breaking capacity of high-voltage vacuum circuit breakers and the beam quality of metal ion sources, yet the underlying ion separation mechanisms during jet mixing remain poorly resolved by existing models. While three-dimensional (3D) particle-fluid hybrid frameworks under the Darwin approximation have been established for vacuum arc simulations, most prior studies neglect strong ion-ion Coulomb collisions in the high-density jet core, which are essential for accurate description of multi-component transport and separation. In this work, we extend this established 3D hybrid framework by incorporating Monte Carlo algorithm for ion collisions, and systematically evaluate spatiotemporal step constraints for highly collisional jet simulations: the minimum spatiotemporal step size should satisfy the ion collision mean free path (~μm) and the resulting time step limit (~10 -14 s). Finally, numerical simulations are carried out for the multi-cathode spot jet process of ZrD vacuum arcs. Simulations reveal that kinetic energy thermalization in the mixing zone is the fundamental driver of light-heavy ion separation: light D ions acquire higher thermal velocities due to mass effects, forming a wide-angle background halo, while heavy Zr ions retain an inertia-dominated central beam. The simulated angular flux distributions and ion kinetic energy peaks (~100 eV for Zr, ~7 eV for D) are in good agreement with time-of-flight experimental measurements. This work provides a physically robust kinetic simulation tool for elucidating multi-component vacuum arc jet mixing mechanisms and optimizing the performance of vacuum arc-based devices.
